authoredSolutions.75: For \(x\in\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\pi\right)\) we have \(\frac{x}{2}\in\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(\sqrt{1+\sin x}=\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}\) and \(\sqrt{1-\sin x}=\sin\frac{x}{2}-\cos\frac{x}{2}\). The argument reduces to \(\frac{2\sin\frac{x}{2}}{2\cos\frac{x}{2}}=\tan\frac{x}{2}=\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{x}{2}\right)\), so \(y=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{x}{2}\) and \(\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{1}{2}\) throughout the interval, in particular at \(x=\frac{5\pi}{6}\). Hence (A).
authoredSolutions.76: The point with ordinate \(3\) is \((2,3)\). Differentiating \((y-2)^{2}=x-1\) gives \(2(y-2)y'=1\), so the slope at \((2,3)\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\) and the tangent is \(x=2y-4\). Integrating with respect to \(y\) from \(0\) to \(3\), the area enclosed by the parabola \(x=(y-2)^{2}+1\), this tangent and the \(x\)-axis is \(9\) square units. Hence (A).
authoredSolutions.90: Write \(2e^{x}+3e^{-x}=A(4e^{x}+7e^{-x})+B(4e^{x}-7e^{-x})\). Matching coefficients gives \(4A+4B=2\) and \(7A-7B=3\), so \(A=\frac{13}{28},\ B=\frac{1}{28}\). The integral becomes \(Ax+B\log_{e}(4e^{x}+7e^{-x})+C=\frac{1}{14}\left(\frac{13}{2}x+\frac12\log_{e}(4e^{x}+7e^{-x})\right)+C\), so \(u=\frac{13}{2},\ v=\frac12\) and \(u+v=7\).
